thread:
anish: Quick heads-up — noticed a potential race when hotset coalescing runs at the same time as a prefix handoff. Saw a spike in `prefix_demote_latency` and a bunch of 503s for a short window.

maya: ugh. can you repro locally or is this in canary?

anish: Canary. Saw it twice in the last 3 hours on the eu-west pool. Repro steps look flaky but pattern is consistent: coalesce job scans hotset -> marks items as coalesced -> handoff starts moving ownership -> eviction path hits a now-coalesced marker and returns a soft-miss, callers end up re-requesting in a tight loop.

sam: is this the coalesce that rewrites residency metadata to attach a `coalesce_version` field? if so maybe the handoff expects an invariant that `residency.version` is monotonic but coalesce does a blind write.

anish: exactly. coalesce currently does `write-if-still-present` but not under the prefix lease. handoff assumes if `residency.owned_by != me` it can proceed. there's a small window where coalesce flips flags and handoff sees inconsistent tombstone -> retries rapidly.

katie: rough sketch of failure:

```
// timeline
T1: coalesce scan -> prepares updates (set coalesced=true)
T2: handoff starts -> reads residency, sees owner=old
T3: coalesce commits update (now coalesced=true, epoch=N)
T4: handoff writes takeover with check owner==old
T5: eviction path sees coalesced marker and treats as not-resident -> returns MISS
```

katie: result = both sides spinning and creating extra load. metric we saw: `kvcache_eviction_retries` bump and `kv_prefix_latency_p50` climb for that tenant.

anish: proposed fix A: make coalesce acquire a lightweight per-prefix lease (same as handoff) so it serializes with handoff. Pros: simple correctness; Cons: could slow coalesce and reduce parallelism.

sam: proposed fix B: make coalesce commit using an atomic read-modify that preserves owner epoch (CAS on `residency.generation`). If CAS fails, coalesce retries or skips.

maya: both seem fine. B seems less invasive perf-wise. question: do we have CAS primitives at that granularity in the residency store? I thought we only had conditional writes on entire prefix key.

anish: we do — `txn.compare_and_set(prefix_key, expected_meta, new_meta)` exists but the coalesce updates are batched and currently sent in bulk with a best-effort path.

katie: also consider C: make eviction/read path tolerant of coalesced markers if takeover is in-flight — i.e., treat coalesced+recent-epoch as potentially transitional and fall back to a slower verification path instead of miss. adds complexity to read path.

sam: I like B + telemetry. CAS ensures minimal contention. If CAS fails a few times we can log a metric `coalesce_cas_conflicts` and skip that prefix this run.

maya: agree. operationally we should add a smoke test harness that simulates coalesce+handoff concurrently using the local acceptance tests. Can we add a new chaos test in the kvcache CI job?

ci-bot: new job queued: `kvcache/coalesce-handoff-chaos` (runs in staging pool, 10 iterations per PR).

anish: awesome. I'll draft the PR: change batched coalesce commit to use per-prefix CAS and on >3 CAS failures mark prefix "deferred" until next run. Also add `coalesce_cas_conflicts` and a logging entry with `prefix_id` and `epoch`.

katie: add an opt-in feature flag `coalesce_serialization_mode=cas` so we can roll out.

sam: rollout plan: merge behind flag -> enable on staging -> run `kvcache/coalesce-handoff-chaos` with flag enabled -> monitor `kvcache_eviction_retries` and `coalesce_cas_conflicts` -> enable in canary -> monitor 1h -> enable global.

maya: can you add a short note in the ops-runbook about manual mitigation: toggle `coalesce_serialization_mode` back to `best-effort` and trigger manual prefix quiesce for the affected pool.

anish: will do. assigning follow-ups:
- anish: PR for CAS commit + metrics + flag (ETA EOD)
- maya: add chaos tests + CI job tweak (ETA tomorrow)
- sam: help vet correctness proofs for CAS path (ETA tomorrow)
- katie: ops-runbook change + dashboard panels (ETA EOD)

sam: one minor thought — make sure CAS includes `coalesced` bit and `generation` in comparison, not just generation, else weird blips.

anish: noted. I'll include a small snippet in PR description with intended txn condition:

```
expected = { owner: X, generation: G, coalesced: false }
new = { owner: X, generation: G, coalesced: true }
txn.compare_and_set(prefix_key, expected, new)
```

maya: if anyone hits the 503 again, paste logs here and ping `@oncall-eng-runtime`.

anish: thanks all. I'll post the PR link here once up.

ci-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/421 (coalesce: CAS commits + telemetry) :white_check_mark:

maya: reviewing now, ty!
